reason: The source shortcut is solver-specific, but its main early-exit gain requires multiple load dimensions: the existing normalized CVRP task format and independent verifier expose only one load dimension. On one-dimensional instances, the base already checks the nonnegative partial delta before the only load-penalty call. A multi-load CVRP input/verification protocol is needed before this PR can count as an active benchmark task.
solver_behavior_hypothesis: For non-exact local-search proposals, a nonnegative accumulated delta cannot become improving after adding nonnegative load penalties. Checking that condition before each dimension's loadPenalty call can skip remaining penalty work. Route::update also avoids constructing/finalizing load segments when the adjacent node is not a reload depot.
causal_chain: Route proposal evaluation first computes distance and distance penalties, then load penalties by dimension, and finally duration/time-window terms. The PR performs the existing non-exact early rejection inside the load-dimension loops, before calculating another dimension's excess-load penalty. Its Route::update change only finalizes a LoadSegment at reload-depot boundaries; ordinary CVRP edges merge the existing segment directly.
structural_trigger: CVRP instances with many local-search node proposals whose accumulated distance delta is already nonnegative before load penalties, plus routes without reload depots so load-segment finalization can be skipped. Include multi-dimensional load and reload-depot controls where the relevant checks must remain active.
activation_probe: On paired pinned builds count candidate delta evaluations, early returns before loadPenalty by dimension, total loadPenalty calls, LoadSegment finalise calls, reload-depot boundaries, and accepted move/objective traces on the public CVRP panel. Instrumented timing is diagnostic only.
instance_selection_rule: Freeze a public CVRP activation panel before hidden runs, stratified by customer count, vehicle count, and local-search neighborhood size. Use the existing hidden published CVRPLIB X and versioned structural-shift CVRP panel for base-only opportunity measurement; preserve all seeds, failures, and timeouts.
workload_exposure_plan: Use the shared PyVRP driver on the ten visible CVRP instances with paired pinned base and PR images. Trace early delta rejection and load-segment operations; independently verify every returned route against original customer coverage, capacity, and distance objective.
mathematical_risk: If a remaining load penalty can be negative, or if exact/non-exact evaluation paths are confused, the early exit could discard an improving move or corrupt objective accounting. A reload boundary skipped by Route::update could corrupt capacity feasibility. Verify load penalties are nonnegative for the rejected branch and exercise reload and multi-load-dimension controls.
independent_check_plan: Run the independent original CVRP route checker on all public and hidden solutions. Run upstream CostEvaluator and Route tests on both source states, including multi-load-dimension and reload-depot controls; retain all normal exact-solve status semantics and heuristic timeouts.
hidden_generalization_plan: Qualify this as an open CVRP optimization task using a one-seed base-only hidden panel at the primary budget. Report the human PR and any coding-agent effects separately; neither is an admission prerequisite.
overlap_review: PyVRP #845 skips duration-segment calculations when no temporal constraint or duration cost can matter; #869 skips load-penalty dimensions when the partial candidate delta already rules out an improvement and avoids unnecessary load-segment finalization. They save different proposal work and retain different constraint controls. PR #701 changes cumulative distance storage, and #962 prunes unpromising candidate visits before entering helper calls; neither is the same inner delta/load computation.
resource_risk: The new branches avoid per-dimension penalty work but may have a small test cost on proposals that proceed to load checks. The result can vary with candidate ordering and load dimension count; report family-level regressions.
